chunks: All that is in the heavens and the earth belongs to God. We had commanded those who received the Book before you, and have commanded you too, to obey the laws of God. Even if you deny, surely all that is in the heavens and the earth belongs to God; and God is self-sufficient and praise-worthy.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of God's ownership of the heavens and earth in relation to human belief?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse underscores the continuity of the divine covenant, linking the monotheistic fidelity of previous Ahl al- Kitab with the Ahl al-Bayt's community. It highlights that God's self-sufficiency (Al-Ghani) serves as the ultimate basis for worship, independent of human gratitude or disbelief. This reinforces the concept that true taqwa is rooted in recognizing God's absolute ownership rather than transactional piety.
